recentItems.title: Calls for Ukraine ceasefire at UN as war dominates General Assembly
recentItems.description:
Donald Trump told the UN General Assembly that he still sees himself as a president of peace and that a deal between Russia and Ukraine could be imminent.

But one day later, Moscow sent its message to the world, striking Kyiv and cities in the Donetsk region in broad daylight, killing at least seven people.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

50 countries at the UN, as well as the European Union have signed a statement supporting Ukraine's call for Russia to join an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, but the United States was not among them. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy urged allies to put more pressure on Moscow to come to the table. 

War has loomed over the UN General Assembly, as Iran responded to Trump almost casually weighing up the option of annihilation during his speech.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian came to New York with a defiant reply that they will not surrender.

recentItems.title: Can the Greens beat Labour in Starmer’s former seat?
recentItems.description:
As the Greens and Labour fight it out in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election what issues are the voters deciding on? 

Labour is trying to hold onto the seat after a by-election was triggered when Sir Keir Starmer announced he was stepping down.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Labour's candidate, the Camden council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali, might normally have been considered the favourite in what's always been a safe seat for the party.

But she's facing a challenge from Green Party leader Zack Polanski, who's hoping to transform his national profile into a seat in parliament.

recentItems.title: Nurse at centre of trans hospital row takes on nursing union
recentItems.description:
Sandie Peggie is at the centre of a second employment tribunal, as the nurse said she felt discriminated against by a union representative after she was suspended following a complaint over her behaviour towards a transgender colleague.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Peggie is accusing the Royal College of Nursing of failing to properly support her because of her beliefs on gender. 

She previously brought a harassment claim against NHS Fife over sharing a changing room with a transgender doctor.
 
The RCN has denied her allegations.

recentItems.title: NEETs crisis: How a new scheme is helping kids in care
recentItems.description:
Young people leaving the care system are among those most at risk of becoming NEET - not in employment, education or training.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Julien Andre was facing an uncertain future when, at 10 years old, he was given a place at boarding school through a charity bursary.

He says the opportunity gave him “each major step, the ticket to go to the next one” - ultimately giving him a future he might not otherwise have had.

recentItems.title: Russian DISINFORMATION: Can Burnham STOP the UK turning into the USA?
recentItems.description:
Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York, Prime Minister Andy Burnham warned of an "insidious campaign" of hostile foreign interference aimed at stoking domestic division and eroding democratic trust. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

To combat the threat, Burnham announced the creation of the National Centre for Information Defence.

In this episode of The Fourcast, Krishnan Guru-Murthy is joined by disinformation expert and author Nina Jankowicz, the Chair of the Intelligence and Security Committee of Parliament, Lord Beamish, as well as the Conservative MP Alicia Kearns.

They discuss the threat posed by Russia to the UK, the role of tech platforms and whether the new unit could risk the censoring of free speech.
